examples.text: Миша, скоро у нас модный показ.
examples.trans: Misha, soon we will have a fashion show.

examples.text: Нам нужно очень хорошо к нему подготовиться.
examples.trans: We need to prepare very well for it.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Моя будущая жена ваша большая поклонница.
examples.trans: My future wife is a big admirer of yours.

examples.text: Моя жена хотела дать большой концерт.
examples.trans: My wife wanted to give a big concert.

examples.text: Подождите, ваша жена большая знаменитость?
examples.trans: Wait, is your wife a big celebrity?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я ещё ничего не сказала Никите.
examples.trans: I have not said anything to Nikita yet.

examples.text: Покормите меня завтра ещё пару раз.
examples.trans: Feed me a couple more times tomorrow.

examples.text: Какой ещё Луи, что ты врёшь?
examples.trans: What do you mean Louis, why are you lying?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'леза'). Common feminine noun meaning 'tears' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Модельер весь день за нами следит.
examples.trans: The designer watches us all day long.

examples.text: После сегодняшнего я ни в чём не уверен.
examples.trans: After today I am not sure of anything.

examples.text: Пробежала вся в слезах?
examples.trans: She ran past all in tears?

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'сохнуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'dried'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и высохнуть вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and dried on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют высохнуть.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to dried.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Девушка, вам уже хватит сегодня пить.
examples.trans: Miss, you have had enough to drink today.

examples.text: Кажется, он уже совсем глухой стал.
examples.trans: It seems he has gone completely deaf already.

examples.text: Ну давай уже скорее награждай нас!
examples.trans: Well come on and reward us quickly already!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'again', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Опять несёте мясо для костюмера?
examples.trans: Are you carrying meat for the costume designer again?

examples.text: Костя, мне скоро опять идти в номер.
examples.trans: Kostya, I have to go back to the room soon.

examples.text: А ты уже опять за старое!
examples.trans: And you are already back to your old tricks!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Отлично, я приеду за день до показа.
examples.trans: Excellent, I will arrive a day before the show.

examples.text: Какой-то странный модельер в отель заехал.
examples.trans: Some strange fashion designer checked into the hotel.

examples.text: Я замуж за тебя в нём пойду!
examples.trans: I will marry you in it!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тарый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('old').

examples.text: Оно напоминает ей о старом времени.
examples.trans: It reminds her of the old days.

examples.text: А ты уже опять за старое!
examples.trans: And you are already back to your old tricks!

examples.text: У меня старый телефон.
examples.trans: I have an old phone.
